purpose: Separate permanent regression coverage from capability-specific user journeys added by each DevSeek convergence iteration.

baseline.test_name: Headless product entry settles five coding fixtures from isolated real workspaces
baseline.claim_limit: Passing these fixed cases proves regression stability only; it cannot prove an iteration's newly implemented capability.

iterations.goal: Converge canonical memory authority and durable checkpoint ownership across product surfaces.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds memory authority, sensitive persistence, legacy-memory migration, sealed prompt projection, and interruption/resume behaviors absent from the five fixed coding fixtures.

cases.user_action: Run a review while an external page attempts to persist an instruction and a user preference is also available.
expected_outcomes: The external instruction is rejected with external-authority-elevation.
The user preference remains memory authority and is the only selected entry.

evidence.test_name: I10-MEM-01 user journey: external memory cannot become an instruction

cases.user_action: Ask DevSeek to persist memory containing a token-shaped secret.
expected_outcomes: The write is rejected before storage even when persistence would otherwise be allowed.
No structured memory record is created.

evidence.test_name: I10-MEM-02 user journey: sensitive persistent memory is blocked before storage

cases.user_action: Open a repository that still contains legacy .devseek/memory.md content.
expected_outcomes: Legacy markdown is not injected into the model prompt automatically.
Migration into structured memory still requires policy evaluation and approval.

evidence.test_name: I10-MEM-03 user journey: legacy markdown never enters prompt context automatically

cases.user_action: Run a canonical VS Code task while an approved user memory and an external instruction-shaped memory are both available.
expected_outcomes: The prompt consumes the kernel's sealed memory decision without reading the store again.
Only the user memory is projected and every projected entry remains explicitly below instruction authority.

evidence.test_name: I10-MEM-04 user journey: VS Code prompt consumes the sealed memory decision exactly once

cases.user_action: Interrupt a two-stage task after the first stage, then resume it in a new run.
expected_outcomes: The sealed checkpoint restores only the pending stage and does not replay the completed stage.
The resumed run is explicitly marked as requiring revalidation.

evidence.test_name: I10-CHK-01 user journey: interrupted work resumes pending units without replay

iterations.goal: Converge canonical context compaction and fail-closed resume idempotency without replaying completed or indeterminate effects.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds three-pass context compaction with sealed task, provenance, memory-policy, progress, evidence, and checkpoint ancestry; adds stable resume operation receipts and replay blocking absent from I10 and the five fixed coding fixtures.

cases.user_action: Run a long task through three context compactions after stale memory and secret-shaped text enter the candidate context.
expected_outcomes: Every pass retains the canonical task, source provenance, rejected memory identity, completed prefix, pending work, evidence, and revalidation requirement.
Receipt and checkpoint ancestry remain continuous while secret and stale-memory content never re-enter the rendered prompt.

evidence.test_name: I11-CMP-01 user journey: three context compactions preserve canonical facts and progress

cases.user_action: Continue a long VS Code tool conversation until history is compacted three times.
expected_outcomes: VS Code inserts the Kernel-sealed context receipt instead of inferring constraints or decisions from prose.
A tampered receipt is rejected before it can be delivered to the provider.

evidence.test_name: I11-CMP-02 user journey: VS Code delivers a sealed context compaction receipt

cases.user_action: Resume the same interrupted workspace edit twice after the first resumed attempt committed it.
expected_outcomes: The stable operation key maps the completed receipt back to the same checkpoint unit.
The second resume skips the committed workspace effect and does not apply it twice.

evidence.test_name: I11-RSM-01 user journey: completed workspace effect is skipped on a second resume

cases.user_action: Retry an interrupted release after the provider disconnected with the external publish result unknown.
expected_outcomes: The indeterminate external-effect receipt blocks the entire replay plan.
The retry is settled blocked before the runtime can repeat the publish.

evidence.test_name: I11-RSM-02 user journey: indeterminate external effect blocks replay before runtime

iterations.goal: Converge one Kernel-owned permission, sandbox, workspace-mutation, external-effect, and receipt-driven resume boundary across product surfaces.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds task-sandbox, forged-Surface-authority, approved-input-substitution, journal-receipt, and resume-operation-substitution denials, a reconciled and idempotent confirmed remote mutation, and a real external-effect receipt that settles and skips only the exact resumed work; none is exercised by I10, I11, or the five fixed coding fixtures.

cases.user_action: Run a read-only repository review while the editor Surface attempts to authorize a workspace write.
expected_outcomes: The immutable review task resolves a read-only sandbox and overrides the Surface's attempted allow.
The canonical denied receipt is retained and the workspace host is never called.

evidence.test_name: I12-AUT-01 user journey: read-only task rejects a Surface-authorized write before host dispatch

cases.user_action: Run an authorized change task through a Headless Surface that attempts to forge the final authorized status.
expected_outcomes: Both a final status hidden in the Surface constraint and a structurally valid foreign receipt are rejected because only the bound Kernel authority session may issue execution authority.
No authorization is recorded by the bound session and the workspace host is never called.

evidence.test_name: I12-AUT-02 user journey: a writable task rejects Surface-issued final authority

cases.user_action: Approve one exact workspace mutation, then let the Surface attempt to reuse its authority receipt for different tool input.
expected_outcomes: The authority receipt binds an immutable semantic digest of the approved input.
Substituted path or content is rejected before host dispatch and no workspace effect occurs.

evidence.test_name: I12-AUT-03 user journey: approved tool input cannot be substituted before host dispatch

cases.user_action: Post an explicitly confirmed implementation result to a remote issue after checking whether that exact effect already exists.
expected_outcomes: The mutation reconciles as not-started before dispatch and produces one committed external-effect receipt.
Repeating the same action identity replays the receipt without a second reconciliation or host call.

evidence.test_name: I12-EFX-01 user journey: confirmed remote mutation reconciles and executes only once

cases.user_action: Resume an interrupted confirmed remote issue update twice after the first resumed run commits it.
expected_outcomes: The actual external-effect receipt directly settles the structured external-effect checkpoint unit as completed.
The next resumed run sees skip-completed and returns prior evidence without reconciling or calling the remote host again.

evidence.test_name: I12-RSM-01 user journey: external effect receipt settles resume and skips the second host call

cases.user_action: Resume a completed remote issue update while attempting to replace its approved comment body with different input.
expected_outcomes: The checkpoint unit and completed receipt remain bound to the exact logical tool operation digest.
The substituted input is rejected before reconciliation, authorization, or remote host dispatch.

evidence.test_name: I12-RSM-02 user journey: completed resume receipt cannot authorize substituted effect input

iterations.goal: Converge provider events, tool schemas, and tool dispatch into shared Kernel-owned ports consumed by every product Surface.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds provider-buffer immutability, canonical schema aliases, fake/native dispatch equivalence, malformed-call rejection, run-scoped workspace dispatch context, protected CLI artifact projection, and conservative unknown-terminal effects; none are exercised by the five fixed coding fixtures.

cases.user_action: Accept a native provider read request, then let the provider mutate its original response buffer before dispatch.
expected_outcomes: The accepted provider event retains the original path as an immutable snapshot.
The canonical dispatcher consumes that snapshot and cannot observe the substituted path.

evidence.test_name: I13-PRV-01 user journey: provider event snapshot survives later provider-buffer mutation

cases.user_action: Use the provider alias search_content with query, directory, and fileTypes arguments.
expected_outcomes: One shared registry resolves the alias to grep_search and normalizes every argument alias.
The internal apply_workspace_artifacts capability stays hidden from the model-visible list.

evidence.test_name: I13-SCH-01 user journey: provider alias resolves through one shared schema registry

cases.user_action: Submit equivalent fake and native search calls followed by a read call missing its required path.
expected_outcomes: Both dialects converge to identical canonical name, input, risk, purpose, and effects.
The incomplete call is rejected with its missing field before any host is called.

evidence.test_name: I13-DSP-01 user journey: fake and native calls converge while incomplete input stops before host

cases.user_action: Receive a truncated native write call, attempt partial normalization wiring, then validate absolute paths inside and outside the current workspace.
expected_outcomes: Malformed arguments produce a rejected non-executable call with no execution evidence.
Partial provider/dispatch wiring fails closed instead of silently selecting a Surface-local fallback.
Fake and native validation calls inherit the same run workspace; an in-workspace absolute path stays validation while an outside path remains high risk.

evidence.test_name: I13-VSC-01 user journey: VS Code rejects invalid wiring and preserves workspace dispatch context

cases.user_action: Return a CLI file artifact targeting .env.local without protected-path approval.
expected_outcomes: The internal artifact dispatch projects .env.local as a protected target before authority evaluation.
The mutation host and verifier are never called.

evidence.test_name: I13-CLI-01 user journey: CLI protected artifact path is denied before workspace mutation

cases.user_action: Return an unfamiliar Ruby maintenance command from the CLI model response.
expected_outcomes: Unknown terminal behavior is conservatively projected as process plus workspace mutation.
CLI authority denies the request and no terminal or workspace host runs.

evidence.test_name: I13-CLI-02 user journey: CLI unknown terminal command is conservatively denied as a workspace effect

iterations.goal: Make tool and side-effect identity process-independent, reconcile durable workspace effects after interruption, and fail closed when only process-local external evidence exists.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds immutable on-disk prepare/settle records, restart-time VS Code and CLI postcondition reconciliation, process-local external-effect refusal, run-global semantic tool identities, and metadata symlink containment; none are exercised by the fixed coding baseline or I10-I13 journeys.

cases.user_action: Resume the same file-read intent in a new agent process, then repeat that intent within one run.
expected_outcomes: The semantic operation digest and first-occurrence action identity remain stable across different run IDs.
Repeated identical actions within one run receive distinct occurrence identities and a run-global sequence.

evidence.test_name: I14-ID-01 user journey: tool identity survives restart and distinguishes same-run repeats

cases.user_action: Resume a VS Code write after the requested content reached disk but the process stopped before recording its terminal receipt.
expected_outcomes: The immutable preparation is loaded by a new transaction instance and the current file is reconciled against the exact desired content.
The result is committed with reconciliation evidence and the host commit method is never called again.

evidence.test_name: I14-VSC-01 user journey: VS Code restart proves the persisted write without applying it twice

cases.user_action: Resume a CLI file creation whose content is durable while its receipt is still only prepared.
expected_outcomes: A new filesystem journal and transaction recover the prepared baseline and prove the exact final content.
The CLI apply host is not invoked a second time and the recovered receipt is committed.

evidence.test_name: I14-CLI-01 user journey: CLI restart recognizes a committed file and skips a second apply

cases.user_action: Resume an interrupted remote publish when its reconciler remembers only process-local state.
expected_outcomes: The stale process-local reconciler is not consulted after restart.
The remote host is not called again and the effect settles indeterminate with a durable-reconciliation-unavailable reason.

evidence.test_name: I14-EXT-01 user journey: restart blocks process-local reconciliation before duplicate dispatch

cases.user_action: Open a workspace whose .devseek metadata entry redirects to an external directory through a symbolic link.
expected_outcomes: Journal preparation rejects the unsafe directory before creating a record.
The external target remains empty.

evidence.test_name: I14-JRN-01 user journey: workspace metadata symlink cannot redirect durable evidence

iterations.goal: Converge requirements, external-source grounding, executable acceptance, design decisions, and effect-authorizing change plans into shared Kernel-owned ports.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds explicit non-goal preservation, exact source-to-boundary receipts, subjective-oracle blocking, immutable design impact and rollback decisions, target/effect plan enforcement, and evidence-bound requirement/plan revision; none are exercised by the fixed coding baseline or I10-I14 journeys.

cases.user_action: Request one exact source change while explicitly forbidding an authentication edit and dependency additions.
expected_outcomes: The requested source change remains a functional requirement.
Both prohibitions remain immutable non-goals and cannot become deliverables.

evidence.test_name: I15-REQ-01 keeps explicit non-goals out of functional deliverables

cases.user_action: Ask for a current API fact, first with no source receipt, then with a source bound to the wrong boundary, and finally with exact official-source receipts.
expected_outcomes: Missing or mismatched source evidence leaves the requirement in exploration-required state.
Only an exact boundary/source match with tool and external-effect receipts becomes grounded and ready.

evidence.test_name: I15-EXT-01 requires exact external-source attribution and preserves effect receipts

cases.user_action: Ask for a code change whose only stated completion test is that it looks good.
expected_outcomes: The subjective oracle is marked weak and requires clarification.
A scoped verification oracle remains executable and ready under the same authority.

evidence.test_name: I15-ACC-01 blocks subjective completion while executable oracles remain ready

cases.user_action: Request a shared-owner refactor with one exact target, focused verification, rollback, and a declared dependency direction.
expected_outcomes: The selected design records alternatives, impact, dependency direction, rollback, and acceptance mappings without mutating the workspace.
The change plan authorizes only the declared target and effects; sibling writes and undeclared git effects are denied.

evidence.test_name: I15-DSN-01 produces an immutable impact, rollback, acceptance, and effect plan

cases.user_action: Revise an unresolved requirement and plan after new evidence, then attempt another revision with an invented evidence reference.
expected_outcomes: A semantic revision retains immutable parent lineage and the exact revision reason.
A no-op revision reuses identity while unbound evidence is rejected.

evidence.test_name: I15-REV-01 requirement revisions require bound evidence and retain parent lineage

iterations.goal: Let natural coding requests discover concrete targets without weakening workspace containment or explicit user scope.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds a shared evidence-bound plan-revision session at Tool Authority: targetless and multi-file proposals become immutable design/plan revisions before effects, while strict scope and workspace escapes fail closed; I10-I15 do not exercise this pre-effect target-discovery path.

cases.user_action: Request a feature and focused test without naming files, then let the tool propose two concrete workspace targets.
expected_outcomes: The targetless initial design and plan are revised before workspace authority is issued.
The final plan retains parent lineage and authorizes exactly both proposed files.

evidence.test_name: I16-RPL-01 tool-proposed targets revise a targetless plan before workspace authority

cases.user_action: Explicitly allow only one file, then receive a tool proposal for a sibling file.
expected_outcomes: The explicit no-other-files scope cannot be widened by provider output.
No new design or plan revision is recorded for the denied proposal.

evidence.test_name: I16-SCP-01 strict user scope cannot be widened by a tool proposal

cases.user_action: Receive a model-proposed path that lexically escapes the active workspace.
expected_outcomes: Workspace projection rejects the path before plan-scope evaluation or host mutation.
The blocked initial plan remains unchanged and the exact outside path is auditable.

evidence.test_name: I16-BND-01 workspace escape is rejected before plan scope evaluation

cases.user_action: Limit implementation to src/**, propose one nested source target, then propose a test target outside that glob.
expected_outcomes: The nested source target produces an evidence-bound ready plan revision.
The later target outside src/** is denied without widening the current plan.

evidence.test_name: I16-GLO-01 strict glob scope admits only matching concrete proposals

iterations.goal: Make completion and settlement Kernel-owned, with verification evidence bound to one run and its exact acceptance contract.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds adversarial Surface terminal claims, foreign-run verification, acceptance substitution, exact bound verification, and failed-then-resolved revalidation; the fixed five coding fixtures and I10-I16 do not exercise these terminal-authority boundaries.

cases.user_action: Let the editor Surface claim completed and submit direct pass evidence without invoking the required verifier.
expected_outcomes: The Surface claim remains ordinary result data and cannot set canonical terminal state.
Kernel completion settles blocked with verification-not-run and no verification receipt.

evidence.test_name: I17-OWN-01 Surface completed claims cannot settle a verification task

cases.user_action: Run the project verifier through the Kernel session for the active run and exact requested acceptance.
expected_outcomes: The session records one evidence-backed passed verification receipt.
Kernel completion and settlement both authorize completed.

evidence.test_name: I17-VRF-01 exact run-bound verification authorizes Kernel completion

cases.user_action: Submit a valid-looking verifier plan whose run ID belongs to another execution.
expected_outcomes: The bound verification session rejects the foreign run before verifier host dispatch.
No receipt is retained and Kernel completion stays blocked.

evidence.test_name: I17-RUN-01 verifier evidence from another run is rejected before host dispatch

cases.user_action: Reuse the active run but replace the requested acceptance statement in the verifier plan.
expected_outcomes: The verification session rejects the drifted acceptance contract before host dispatch.
No receipt is retained and direct Surface evidence cannot close the task.

evidence.test_name: I17-ACC-01 verifier cannot substitute a different acceptance contract

cases.user_action: Observe a failed focused check, apply one repair, then rerun the same acceptance scope successfully.
expected_outcomes: Both failed and passed receipts remain auditable while the later pass explicitly resolves the earlier action.
Only the unresolved evidence enters completion, allowing a completed settlement after repair.

evidence.test_name: I17-RPR-01 passed revalidation resolves the failed pre-repair evidence

iterations.goal: Converge verifier selection, build orchestration, and independent verification into one factual, read-only, acceptance-bound pipeline across all product Surfaces.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds strongest scoped verifier selection, source-mutation detection, structural readback separation, immutable pre-existing verifier enforcement, unavailable-host suppression, and unknown-extension text classification; none are established by the fixed five coding fixtures or I10-I17.

cases.user_action: Offer multiple verifier capabilities for one scoped source change, including a stronger read-only project check and weaker or mutable alternatives.
expected_outcomes: The acceptance-bound selector chooses the strongest eligible read-only capability with exact scope coverage.
Candidate priority cannot bypass verifier identity, scope, or workspace-access constraints.

evidence.test_name: I18-SEL-01 user journey: acceptance selects the strongest scoped read-only verifier

cases.user_action: Run a verifier that exits zero but rewrites the source file it is supposed to inspect.
expected_outcomes: Build orchestration records the workspace mutation and settles indeterminate.
The zero exit code cannot be converted into passing independent verification.

evidence.test_name: I18-BLD-01 user journey: source-mutating verifier cannot produce a passing receipt

cases.user_action: Commit and independently read back the requested file while keeping project verification as a separate acceptance oracle.
expected_outcomes: Committed path-bound readback satisfies only workspace structural acceptance.
No verification or external-source acceptance is fabricated from the mutation receipt.

evidence.test_name: I18-ACC-01 user journey: committed readback satisfies structural acceptance without claiming verification

cases.user_action: Ask CLI to repair a C++ program while a pre-existing project verifier requires exact stdout that the first generated source does not produce.
expected_outcomes: The model cannot weaken or replace the pre-existing verifier configuration.
The first check fails, one bounded repair adds the missing behavior, and revalidation passes.

evidence.test_name: I18-CLI-01 user journey: pre-existing project verifier cannot be weakened by generated source

cases.user_action: Invoke Headless verification for a required acceptance criterion without supplying an applicable verifier capability.
expected_outcomes: Selection and orchestration remain unavailable without dispatching the host.
Independent verification settles unverified and cannot authorize completion.

evidence.test_name: I18-HDL-01 user journey: unavailable Headless verifier never dispatches the host

cases.user_action: Create an explicitly requested plain-text artifact whose filename uses an unknown extension.
expected_outcomes: VS Code classifies the committed content from bytes instead of guessing from the extension.
Canonical file readback passes without inventing a build script or running a process.

evidence.test_name: I18-VSC-01 user journey: unknown-extension text completes from factual readback

iterations.goal: Converge code-change conformance, causal integration evidence, diagnostic normalization, regression selection, and bounded adaptive repair into one cross-Surface Kernel pipeline.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds plan-versus-mutation settlement, direct-write bypass detection, stable path-bound diagnostic fingerprints, dependency-aware and full-risk regression selection, one root-cause replan, and repeated-mutation early stop; none are established by the fixed five coding fixtures or I10-I18.

cases.user_action: Apply exactly the accepted source target through a committed transaction with matching readback evidence.
expected_outcomes: The changed path covers the accepted change-plan target.
Code-change conformance settles only after committed readback evidence exists.

evidence.test_name: I19-CHG-01 user journey: planned code change requires committed readback evidence

cases.user_action: Commit the requested source change together with an undeclared sibling path.
expected_outcomes: The extra path is reported as unplanned even though the transaction committed.
The code-change decision fails closed instead of treating commit status as sufficient.

evidence.test_name: I19-CHG-02 user journey: committed unplanned paths fail code change conformance

cases.user_action: Execute a planned write through one authorized tool action, commit its transaction, and verify the same changed scope.
expected_outcomes: Tool, mutation, and verification receipts form one action-bound causal chain.
No changed path remains unverified or detached from tool execution.

evidence.test_name: I19-INT-01 user journey: tool mutation and verification form one causal chain

cases.user_action: Present a committed workspace mutation without the matching completed mutating-tool receipt.
expected_outcomes: The mutation is identified as bypassing canonical tool execution.
Verification cannot repair the missing causal authority chain.

evidence.test_name: I19-INT-02 user journey: direct mutation bypass cannot authorize completion

cases.user_action: Receive a TypeScript verifier failure that identifies an affected source path and acceptance criterion.
expected_outcomes: The failure becomes one stable typecheck diagnosis bound to the affected path.
The same receipt replays the same immutable diagnostic decision and fingerprint.

evidence.test_name: I19-DGN-01 user journey: verifier failure becomes a stable path-bound diagnosis

cases.user_action: Repair a failed downstream verifier after ordered prerequisite checks already ran.
expected_outcomes: Regression selection reruns the ordered prerequisite prefix through the failed check.
Acceptance coverage is preserved while unrelated checks remain excluded.

evidence.test_name: I19-REG-01 user journey: repair reruns failed verification with ordered prerequisites

cases.user_action: Change infrastructure configuration together with source code after a failed validation.
expected_outcomes: Configuration risk expands selection to the full applicable verifier set.
A narrowly targeted retry cannot conceal infrastructure-wide regression risk.

evidence.test_name: I19-REG-02 user journey: infrastructure changes expand to full risk verification

cases.user_action: Submit two different repairs for the same normalized TypeScript diagnosis, with the second repair changing the root-cause hypothesis.
expected_outcomes: The first diagnosis permits a retry and one repeated diagnosis requests root-cause replanning.
Changed repair evidence is reverified and the third attempt completes.

evidence.test_name: I19-RPR-01 user journey: one root-cause replan lets changed repair evidence succeed

cases.user_action: Return the identical repair response after the same verifier diagnosis repeats.
expected_outcomes: The repeated mutation and diagnosis settle as no progress.
The loop blocks before spending another provider repair turn.

evidence.test_name: I19-RPR-02 user journey: identical repair stops before another provider turn

iterations.goal: Separate implementation from independent review and bind delivery, release, observation, and rollback to exact evidence identities.
iterations.delta_from_baseline: Adds self-review rejection, complete changed-scope review, introduced-finding severity, source-bound artifacts, review-bound Git effects, immutable delivery manifests, explicit release authorization, ordered CI/deploy/smoke/observe identity, and exact rollback targets; none is covered by the fixed five coding fixtures or I10-I19.

cases.user_action: Ask a separate reviewer to inspect all changed paths after implementation, while the implementation actor first attempts to self-review and then leaves an introduced important finding open.
expected_outcomes: Self-review and incomplete changed-path coverage are indeterminate rather than accepted.
A verified open important finding introduced by the change vetoes delivery.

evidence.test_name: I20-REV-01 user journey: independent review rejects self-review, incomplete scope, and open introduced findings

cases.user_action: Build an artifact from one commit and request a reviewed push, then present a stale artifact, a self-reported push without effect receipt, and a mismatched review fingerprint.
expected_outcomes: Artifact identity fails on source-commit drift and Git delivery rejects missing external-effect evidence.
Only the exact passed review fingerprint and committed Git effect can enter a ready immutable delivery manifest.

evidence.test_name: I20-DLV-01 user journey: exact artifact and reviewed Git evidence govern delivery

cases.user_action: Authorize one ready manifest for release and carry its artifact identity through CI, deploy, smoke, and observation, including one stale smoke-stage identity attempt.
expected_outcomes: A release request without explicit authorization remains blocked even when its manifest is ready.
Stages must be ordered and bind the same artifact; stale identity becomes indeterminate and the exact chain passes.

evidence.test_name: I20-REL-01 user journey: authorized release preserves artifact identity through observation

cases.user_action: Observe a smoke failure after deployment, first omit rollback target and authority, then execute an authorized rollback to one exact previous artifact.
expected_outcomes: A post-deploy failure makes rollback required and blocks an unspecified or unauthorized recovery.
Rollback completes only with a committed release-effect receipt bound to the exact target artifact.

evidence.test_name: I20-RBK-01 user journey: post-deploy failure requires exact authorized rollback
